newsitem.title: USA: NIMO 9 Mile Pt nuke seen back by weekend.
newsitem.headline: NIMO 9 Mile Pt nuke seen back by weekend.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp's (NIMO) 610 megawatt Nine Mile Point nuclear power unit 1 tripped off line late Tuesday due to a generator problem, and was expected to resume power production by the weekend, a spokesman said.
"We still have some checking to do, but it should return to service over the weekend," spokesman Alberto Bianchetti said Wednesday.
NIMO was evaluating a generator malfunction, and also intended to do some additional maintenance to the unit while it was shut down, Bianchetti said.
NIMO should be able to meet its power demand despite the cut in generation, the spokesman said.

"We are in pretty good shape, we have an excess of capacity for Niagara and the state as a whole," Bianchetti said, adding that autumn power demand was comparatively low measured against summer and winter peaks.
The 1,137 megawatt Nine Mile Point nuclear power unit 2, also at Scriba, was operating at 93 percent of capacity and increasing power as of early Wednesday, Bianchetti said.
Nine Mile Point 2 was on its way back to full power from a scheduled maintenance outage which began September 28.
The Nine Mile Point units are operated by NIMO, which holds 100 percent ownership of unit 1 and a 41 percent stake in unit 2.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
